use_case: Tailgating detection: counts people passing each lobby turnstile lane against badge reads and alerts the RSOC and lobby desk with a clip
vendor_or_model: Access control and video platform vendor (computer-vision person-detection model)
data_categories: Video of lobby turnstile lanes; turnstile badge events; alert clips (no face templates; no identity inferred)
consequential_decision_category: None directly (advisory alerts); becomes Safety/CI if alerts drive automatic turnstile or door actions
human_in_the_loop: An officer reviews the clip and badge record before any action; the only permitted action is a courteous badge check; accessible-lane alerts are review-only
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) and the FTC biometric policy statement (2023-05-18); CCPA notice at collection for the 8 California lobbies (Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100(a)); 11 CCR 7150(b)(6) if the vendor trains on company video; state privacy laws (video is excluded from biometric data in Fla. Stat. 501.702, worked example)
cppa_obligation: Notice at collection update for California lobbies (P03 G-067); written training opt-out for the West tenant (P03 G-075)
bias_testing_status: Lane-level false alert testing: accessible-lane disparity found (3.4 times the baseline); skin tone and clothing not testable in the alert sample
monitoring: Monthly 300-alert precision sample; quarterly staged recall test at 6 lobbies; monthly accessible-lane false alert ratio

use_case: Face verification express lane: compares a live face capture at the turnstile with the enrolled photo of a tenant employee who opted in, and opens the lane on a match
vendor_or_model: Access control and video platform vendor (face recognition model)
data_categories: Face templates from enrolled photos and live captures (treated as biometric data); badge events
human_in_the_loop: Opt-in only; badge-only lanes stay open for everyone; a non-match never denies entry by itself: the lane stays closed and the person badges in normally or an officer checks the badge
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 and the FTC biometric policy statement; Fla. Stat. 501.171 and 501.702 (whether templates from camera video are biometric data is unsettled; treated as biometric data; counsel to confirm); CCPA 11 CCR 7150(b)(2) and 1798.140(ae)(2)(A) before any California use; other states' biometric laws before any expansion (counsel state review)
cppa_obligation: Risk assessment required before any California use (7150(b)(2)); none in California today
bias_testing_status: Local volunteer study (320 employees): false rejection rate disparity by self-reported skin tone (3.2 times) and age 60+ (2.9 times) above the 1.5 threshold; false match rate vendor-reported only
monitoring: Monthly false rejection rate by lane; quarterly volunteer accuracy study; template count reconciled to enrollments weekly

use_case: License plate recognition at 84 garages operated by 3 parking operators; plate reads shared with the company for permit enforcement and security investigations
data_categories: Plate images, plate numbers, times, and garage locations
human_in_the_loop: RSOC investigators query plate data only with a case number; operators enforce permits
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5; CCPA (California garages; notice at collection); state ALPR and privacy laws (counsel list)
cppa_obligation: Notice at collection at California garages to be confirmed
monitoring: Quarterly review of company queries against case numbers

use_case: BAS energy optimization: a machine-learning service writes chiller and air handler setpoints to Platform A at 40 towers to cut energy use
data_categories: BAS trend data (temperatures, run status, meters); no personal information
human_in_the_loop: Field controllers enforce setpoint limits; Building Technology Directors hold a kill switch; engineers review weekly changes; write path through the OT gateway
bias_testing_status: Not applicable (no individuals); comfort complaints tracked by floor
monitoring: Weekly setpoint change report; quarterly limit review and kill-switch test

data_categories: Leases (business terms; names of signatories and personal guarantors)

applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (vendor claims); contract confidentiality
cppa_obligation: None identified (no significant decision about consumers)

use_case: Security officer scheduling and post assignment optimization
business_owner: Chief Human Resources Officer (with the Vice President, Corporate Security)
data_categories: Officer availability, skills, certifications, overtime, post locations
human_in_the_loop: Supervisors approve generated schedules but rarely change them; redesign or ADMT notices required (POAM-023)
applicable_laws: CCPA ADMT rules (11 CCR 7200 et seq.; compliance by 2027-01-01 for California officers); California Civil Rights Council automated-decision system regulations (2 CCR 11008 et seq.); federal equal employment opportunity laws
cppa_obligation: Possible ADMT for a significant decision (P03 G-077); decision due 2026-10-31
bias_testing_status: Not assessed (planned: assignment of overtime and night posts by sex, age band, and race where recorded)

data_categories: Officer location traces, tour scans, badge events, video clips

applicable_laws: CCPA 11 CCR 7150(b)(4) (risk assessment before California use); state workplace monitoring notice laws (counsel list); federal equal employment opportunity laws
cppa_obligation: No California use before a risk assessment (P03 G-074)
